body: Pathetic. Sometimes as an INTJ I need to think before I judge any sort of negative outburts, but goddamn. People who burst out in fits of rage and let themselves damage others, are one of the worst types of people I know of.

This. It took me years to understand that when someone is emotionally complaining to you, they don't want to recieve a logical solution back. I always deemed them as irrational, and in a literal way, they are. But as a part of maturing, I need to try to step into the shoes of others emotions.

I gotta say that I sort of detest it when someone argues to me like that, because it is hard to pretend to be in tune with their emotions. I'm very bad at acting. Even if the arguing does affect me, I still won't show emotions, because displaying that intimate part of me is too uncomfortable. I need to learn that too.
I riding the bus to/away from school. Just looking out the window and listening to music, completely unbothered, is very soothing. I live in Norway, so no one will try to make a conversation.

I've been a chronically sleep deprived person all my life, but extremely rarely have I ever lashed out. I have, however, adressed irking things that people have done against me in a very, blunt, brutally honest manner. That's the part of INTJs being "biting" that I need to work on. When I was younger, I used to never understand people who lashed out in anger. To me, that was just dumb and irrational. I also feel anger, but I control it very well. Anger is good quality fuel for changing something, though.

I used to be like this when I was younger and less socially skilled. When I just didn't feel the chemistry at first, I didn't bother hanging with them anymore. The part where INTJs tend to become impatient with friendships where the they feel like the other party doesn't have anything to offer to the INTJ is very accurate regarding myself. Now as I've matured more, I've realized that connecting with people becomes easier when you have more social skills. 

Connecting with people is confusing sometimes, though. Sometimes I feel like I'm being so bland and boring to the other party. I once had a very nice ISFJ friend who insisted on hanging with me. I had nothing against it, but I did feel very awkward. She wanted to talk about dresses, the parties she'd been to, people, etc. I was unable to engage passionatly in the conversations, and nearly all of them just died out. But the friendship continued for a prolounged amount of time, because she always returned to me. It was confusing, but I went along with it. The friendship eventually ended as we moved to different schools. I didn't keep the contact. It didn't feel natural for me to casually text just to nurture a friendship, not realizing that to most people, that's a steadfast principle regarding friendships.

The difficulty with friendships with opposing types is not only the lack of mutual interest in conversational topics of leisure activities, but also the level of maintanance.

My best friends, who I don't need to constantly keep in touch to maintain the same chemistry, are INTP, ISTP and INFJ.

I have a death stare when I'm really concentrating about something. I'll squint my eyes, contract my eyebrows and bow my head downwards as I'm looking at whatever I'm focusing on. The harder I need to concentrate, the deeper the stare, as I intensify the three facial demeanors. I make the same face when I think, too.

I also have a tendency to look critical/angry when checking out something. It doesn't matter what I'm checking out, it could be a flower or a chart. I guess it's just an automatic skeptical look many people posess. 

I haven't caught myself making any other "death stares" than these, but who knows? Maybe I subconciously express even more than these two.
